title: How steep is a strong link?
hook: Change the outcome’s units and compare slope with correlation.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: correlation measures tightness, not slope; a near-flat line can have r = 0.99.

misconception: Treating strong but flat as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: correlation measures tightness, not slope; a near-flat line can have r = 0.99.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: The points x=1,2,3 and y=.01,.02,.03 lie on one line. What happens to correlation when y is multiplied by 1,000?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-strong-but-flat/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: x=[1,2,3], y=[.01,.02,.03] gives r=1, slope .01. Rescale y to [10,20,30]: r still1, slope10. Learner changes units, not association tightness.

claims.text: Both cases retain correlation 1, while the slopes are 0.01 and 10. Rescaling the outcome changes its units but preserves the points’ perfect linear ordering.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-strong-but-flat/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: x=[1,2,3], y=[.01,.02,.03] gives r=1, slope .01. Rescale y to [10,20,30]: r still1, slope10. Learner changes units, not association tightness.

claims.text: Correlation normalizes covariance by both variables’ standard deviations. Slope keeps the units of outcome per predictor, so a near-flat line can still have perfect correlation. The axes show their own scales.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-strong-but-flat/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: x=[1,2,3], y=[.01,.02,.03] gives r=1, slope .01. Rescale y to [10,20,30]: r still1, slope10. Learner changes units, not association tightness.

claims.text: Convert a positive straight-line outcome from meters to centimeters. What happens to Pearson correlation? Positive unit rescaling changes slope but leaves normalized correlation unchanged.
